reading.en: The example has the form of the coarsening law: something can end under a finer class (the pot) and not end under a coarser (gold); the three onlookers read three classes. Stated of the real as such, the three marks hold here only relative to classes: under one class they exclude each other, so 'at once' needs two, and no class is warranted. That conditions a universal claim: scope, as for satkārya and anekānta. The Jain substance is a real kind with a nature; the account's class is supplied. The law forbids no pair of classes, and no live text draws this join. [AI reading]

rulings.why: The source predicates the three marks of the real as such; continuation-relative-to-a-class (laws 2, 3) makes them class-relative and warrants no class, as its siblings cx-oi-satkarya and cx-oi-anekanta read the same law (scope); a root law admitting any two classes gives little agreement.
